implementationAcceptance: pending; no implementation or native GUI qualification conducted
scope: OpenSpec taskbar, shell-experience, switcher and window-policy capability deltas
confirmed: Native authority versus Elm presentation ownership is clear.
Minimized enumeration is separated from live scene/input eligibility.
Normal workspace identity, modal drafts, stale incarnation rejection and rollback are explicit.
Optional compositor replacement is appropriately separated from mandatory shell delivery.
GPU discovery and actual accelerated webview/WebGPU qualification are correctly distinct.

findings.title: Cross-workspace activation and taskbar click semantics remain unspecified
findings.counterexample: On workspace 1 the user selects the retained taskbar preview of minimized A on workspace 2. A can be restored on workspace 2 with no workspace switch, so its native receipt passes UX-008 while the user sees no response. Different display views can also choose incompatible behavior for the same target. The contract does not define active-window taskbar clicks, group selection, MRU ordering or which workspaces the switcher enumerates.
findings.proposedEars: The desktop experience inventory SHALL define default and supported preference policies for taskbar click states, group selection, switcher ordering and workspace/output scope, and cross-workspace activation before those interactions are implemented.

scenarioChanges.given: workspace 1 is current and minimized target A belongs to workspace 2
scenarioChanges.when: the user selects A through the taskbar using the frozen activation policy
scenarioChanges.then: one correlated operation makes A visible and focused according to that policy, normal workspace membership is preserved, and all display projections agree

scenarioChanges.given: one active window, one inactive window and a grouped application on the current workspace
scenarioChanges.when: the interaction-table fixtures exercise each taskbar click state and switcher traversal
scenarioChanges.then: each resulting minimize, activate, restore or group-opening action matches the frozen table and produces no duplicate effect

findings.title: Native operation states lack a uniform user-visible recovery contract
findings.counterexample: A pin request remains Pending or Unknown after the authority disconnects. The existing pin indicator correctly waits for correlated observations, but the user sees no feedback and repeatedly clicks. Launch and transfer refusals have feedback; minimize, restore, pin and snap do not uniformly require it or a recovery path.
findings.proposedEars: WHEN a user-requested shell operation is pending, refused or unknown, the shell SHALL expose accessible operation status and a permitted recovery action without asserting success before native confirmation or resending an uncertain mutation.

scenarioChanges.given: a pin request becomes Unknown during authority disconnection
scenarioChanges.when: the user inspects status or invokes recovery
scenarioChanges.then: the UI announces uncertainty, retains last confirmed pin state, reconciles before any new effect and does not replay the old mutation

scenarioChanges.given: a snap or minimize operation receives a terminal refusal
scenarioChanges.then: the shell provides a concise accessible reason and safe next action while preserving native-confirmed state and keyboard focus

findings.phase: P3 shared status / P5 complete surfaces

findings.title: Output removal reconciles generations without guaranteeing reachable controls
findings.counterexample: A keyboard-focused settings popup is on an external output when it is disconnected. Old generations are invalidated correctly and ownership reconciles, but the popup can remain logically focused with no visible surface on the surviving output. A window can also reconcile to off-screen placement.
findings.proposedEars: WHEN an output disappears, the native host SHALL apply a documented surviving-output recovery policy that keeps shell controls and application recovery actions reachable, resolves displaced popup focus and preserves window workspace identity.

scenarioChanges.given: a focused settings popup and an application recovery control occupy the removed external display
scenarioChanges.then: the popup is dismissed with eligible focus restoration or rehosted on the declared surviving output, and application recovery remains keyboard reachable with no invisible focus trap

scenarioChanges.given: all configured outputs disappear and later one returns
scenarioChanges.then: shell controls recover on the available output under the same policy without effects against removed generations

findings.title: First-use discovery and preference migration are not specified
findings.counterexample: The feature selector successfully switches one qualified component and preserves the prior settings file, but a user cannot discover the new Task View/snap shortcuts or find rollback without a working Elm host. Existing shortcut collisions can silently change muscle memory even though settings persistence passes.
findings.proposedEars: WHEN a user first enables a migrated component, the shell SHALL offer dismissible keyboard-accessible guidance for changed interactions, preserve approved existing preferences and expose the documented offline recovery route without requiring onboarding completion.

scenarioChanges.given: an existing Omarchy profile with customized shortcuts and a qualified replacement component
scenarioChanges.when: the user enables it and dismisses first-use guidance
scenarioChanges.then: the existing preference mapping or explicit conflict decision is preserved, new actions remain discoverable in help/settings and the component works without mandatory onboarding

scenarioChanges.given: first-use guidance is dismissed and the Elm host later fails
scenarioChanges.when: the user follows the documented recovery route
scenarioChanges.then: the predecessor can be restored offline and the preserved compatible preferences remain usable

findings.title: User acceptance does not define evidence-based usability criteria
findings.counterexample: An engineer demonstrates every named flow and all native assertions pass, but first-time users cannot discover pin, recover from a refusal or understand a historical preview. The current user gate can pass without recording assistance, confusion, completion time, failures or the user cohorts whose accessibility needs are in scope.
findings.proposedEars: The product verifier SHALL freeze representative usability tasks, participant profiles, assistance rules and measurable success thresholds before candidate evaluation, and SHALL block usability acceptance when required outcomes lack observed evidence.

scenarioChanges.given: a frozen protocol covering novice and experienced desktop users and declared keyboard or assistive-technology routes
scenarioChanges.when: participants attempt taskbar restore, switcher selection, pin, snap, failed-operation recovery and rollback discovery
scenarioChanges.then: task success, assistance, errors, recovery and completion measures are recorded against the predeclared thresholds; failed or unobserved required outcomes block usability acceptance

scenarioChanges.given: a candidate fails a usability threshold
scenarioChanges.then: the failure remains recorded and any changed threshold requires a new documented protocol before a separately identified rerun

findings.phase: P0 protocol / P5 formative / P6 gate

limitations: Read-only planning review, not empirical user research.
The reviewed registry may be superseded by later corrections; this verdict applies to the recorded hash.
No external web sources were required: findings derive from explicit local contracts and counterexamples, not claims about current Windows behavior.
